title: CYP/transporter roles and hand-curated supplement interaction flags
licence: Enzyme and transporter role assignments are taken from the FDA Drug Development and Drug Interactions substrate/inhibitor/inducer tables, a US Government work in the public domain. Supplement, food and lifestyle entries are hand-curated and each carries its own prose citation. No licence-restricted commercial interaction database contributed to this file; docs/mechanism.md names every source that was ruled out and why.
boundaryNote: This is a mechanism flag, not advice. It states a documented mechanism by which one member could change another's exposure or effect; it does not say the interaction will occur, how large it would be, or what anyone should take. There is no severity score here on purpose.
coverageNote: A flag list is bounded by this pack. A member BioCAD does not know is reported in unknownMembers rather than silently dropped, and an empty flag list means nothing in this pack matched - not that the combination is safe.

members.name: Selegiline
members.citation: Selegiline is MAO-B selective at low dose and loses selectivity as dose rises; the mechanism class is stated in its FDA label.

members.name: Moclobemide
members.citation: Moclobemide is a reversible MAO-A inhibitor; the mechanism class is stated in its product information.

members.name: Linezolid
members.citation: Linezolid is a weak reversible MAO inhibitor; the mechanism and the resulting serotonergic caution are stated in its FDA label.

members.name: Sumatriptan
members.citation: Sumatriptan is a 5-HT1B/1D agonist; the mechanism class is stated in its FDA label.

members.name: Levothyroxine
members.citation: Levothyroxine absorption is reduced by polyvalent cations and by binding agents; the interaction is stated in its FDA label.

members.name: Tetracycline
members.citation: Tetracyclines chelate polyvalent cations, reducing absorption; the interaction is stated in the FDA label.

members.name: Tizanidine

members.name: Grapefruit juice
members.citation: Grapefruit furanocoumarins (bergamottin and 6',7'-dihydroxybergamottin) cause mechanism-based inactivation of intestinal CYP3A4 and inhibit intestinal OATP; the interaction and its mechanism are described in FDA labelling guidance and in the grapefruit-juice interaction literature.

members.name: Seville (sour) orange juice
members.citation: Seville orange juice contains the same furanocoumarins as grapefruit and shows the same intestinal CYP3A4 mechanism-based inactivation in the interaction literature.

members.name: Bitter orange (Citrus aurantium, synephrine)
members.citation: Bitter orange extracts supply p-synephrine, an adrenergic agonist/releasing amine; the pharmacology is described in the sympathomimetic supplement literature.

members.name: St John's wort (Hypericum perforatum)
members.citation: Hyperforin is a potent PXR agonist and induces CYP3A4 and P-gp; St John's wort is the FDA table's index herbal inducer, and its serotonergic activity is described in the herb-drug interaction literature.

members.name: Quercetin
members.citation: Quercetin inhibits CYP3A4 and intestinal OATP in vitro; the flavonoid-transporter interaction literature describes both.

members.name: EGCG (epigallocatechin gallate)
members.citation: Green tea catechins including EGCG inhibit intestinal OATP1A2/OATP2B1 uptake; described in the green-tea/nadolol interaction literature.

members.name: Green tea extract
members.citation: Concentrated green tea catechins inhibit intestinal OATP uptake; described in the green-tea/nadolol interaction literature.

members.name: Piperine (black pepper alkaloid)
members.citation: Piperine inhibits CYP3A4 and P-gp and slows glucuronidation, which is the documented basis of its use as a bioavailability enhancer.

members.name: Black pepper
members.citation: Black pepper is the dietary source of piperine; see the piperine entry.

members.name: Curcumin (turmeric)
members.citation: Curcumin inhibits CYP3A4, UGTs and P-gp in vitro and has antiplatelet activity; described in the curcumin pharmacokinetic-interaction literature.

members.name: Resveratrol
members.citation: Resveratrol inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 in vitro and inhibits platelet aggregation; described in the stilbene interaction literature.

members.name: Naringenin / naringin
members.citation: Naringin and naringenin inhibit intestinal OATP; they are NOT the principal cause of the grapefruit CYP3A4 effect, which is furanocoumarin-driven.

members.name: Ginkgo biloba
members.citation: Ginkgolides have antiplatelet activity and ginkgo has shown CYP2C19 induction in interaction studies; described in the ginkgo herb-drug interaction literature.

members.name: Panax ginseng
members.citation: Ginsenosides show antiplatelet activity and ginseng-warfarin interaction reports exist; described in the ginseng herb-drug interaction literature.

members.name: Garlic extract (allicin, ajoene)
members.citation: Garlic organosulfur compounds inhibit platelet aggregation and garlic has shown intestinal CYP3A4/P-gp effects (saquinavir interaction study); described in the garlic interaction literature.

members.name: Echinacea
members.citation: Echinacea has shown CYP1A2 inhibition and hepatic CYP3A induction in a probe-cocktail interaction study; described in the echinacea interaction literature.

members.name: Milk thistle (silymarin, silybin)
members.citation: Silybin inhibits UGTs and CYP2C9 in vitro; described in the silymarin interaction literature.

members.name: Kava (Piper methysticum)
members.citation: Kavalactones inhibit CYP2E1 and other CYPs in probe-cocktail studies; described in the kava interaction literature.

members.name: Valerian
members.citation: Valerian extracts modulate GABA-A signalling; probe-cocktail studies found no clinically meaningful CYP effect, which is recorded here as an absence rather than as a CYP role.

members.name: Chamomile (apigenin)
members.citation: Apigenin inhibits CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 in vitro; described in the flavone interaction literature.

members.name: Licorice (glycyrrhizin)
members.citation: Glycyrrhetinic acid inhibits 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2, producing apparent mineralocorticoid excess; described in the licorice pharmacology literature.

members.name: Goldenseal (Hydrastis, berberine/hydrastine)
members.citation: Goldenseal inhibited CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 in a human probe-cocktail interaction study; described in the goldenseal interaction literature.

members.name: Berberine
members.citation: Berberine inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 and interacts with P-gp in vitro; described in the berberine interaction literature.

members.name: Ginger
members.citation: Gingerols inhibit thromboxane synthesis and platelet aggregation in vitro; described in the ginger pharmacology literature.

members.name: Grape seed extract
members.citation: Proanthocyanidin-rich grape seed extract inhibits CYP3A4 in vitro; described in the polyphenol interaction literature.

members.name: Cranberry juice
members.citation: Cranberry juice has been reported to inhibit CYP2C9 in vitro with mixed clinical findings, and warfarin case reports exist; described in the cranberry interaction literature.

members.name: Pomegranate juice
members.citation: Pomegranate juice inhibits CYP3A4 in vitro; clinical findings are inconsistent, which is stated rather than resolved here.

members.name: Schisandra chinensis
members.citation: Schisandra lignans inhibit CYP3A4 and P-gp; described in the schisandra interaction literature.

members.name: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera)
members.citation: Ashwagandha has reported thyrotropic and GABAergic activity; the CYP position is not established, which is stated rather than filled in.

members.name: Rhodiola rosea
members.citation: Rhodiola extracts inhibit CYP3A4 and P-gp in vitro and salidroside/rosavin fractions show MAO inhibition in vitro; described in the Rhodiola interaction literature.

members.name: Bacopa monnieri
members.citation: Bacoside-rich extracts inhibit CYP3A4 in vitro; described in the Bacopa interaction literature.

members.name: 5-HTP (5-hydroxytryptophan)
members.citation: 5-HTP is decarboxylated to serotonin; the precursor route is basic monoamine biochemistry.

members.name: L-tryptophan
members.citation: Tryptophan is hydroxylated to 5-HTP and decarboxylated to serotonin; the precursor route is basic monoamine biochemistry.

members.name: SAM-e (S-adenosylmethionine)
members.citation: SAM-e is the methyl donor for COMT-mediated catecholamine methylation; serotonergic case reports exist and are described in the SAM-e literature.

members.name: Yohimbine
members.citation: Yohimbine is an alpha-2 adrenoceptor antagonist cleared substantially by CYP2D6; described in the yohimbine clinical-pharmacology literature.

members.name: Ephedra (ephedrine alkaloids)
members.citation: Ephedrine alkaloids are indirect sympathomimetic releasing agents; described in the sympathomimetic pharmacology literature.

members.name: Syrian rue / harmala alkaloids (harmine, harmaline)
members.citation: Harmine and harmaline are reversible MAO-A inhibitors; described in the beta-carboline pharmacology literature.

members.name: Tyramine-rich food (aged cheese, cured meat, fermented soy)
members.citation: Dietary tyramine is an indirect sympathomimetic normally cleared by intestinal MAO-A; the pressor interaction with MAO inhibitors is stated on MAO-inhibitor FDA labels.

members.name: Fish oil (EPA/DHA)
members.citation: Long-chain omega-3 fatty acids reduce platelet aggregation; described in the omega-3 haemostasis literature.

members.name: High-dose vitamin E
members.citation: High-dose alpha-tocopherol has antiplatelet activity and interacts with vitamin K-dependent clotting; described in the vitamin E haemostasis literature.

members.name: Vitamin K (phytonadione, K-rich greens)
members.citation: Vitamin K supply directly opposes vitamin K antagonists; the interaction is stated on the warfarin FDA label.

members.name: Calcium supplement
members.citation: Divalent calcium chelates tetracyclines and fluoroquinolones and reduces levothyroxine absorption; the interaction is stated on those FDA labels.

members.name: Magnesium supplement
members.citation: Divalent magnesium chelates tetracyclines and fluoroquinolones; the interaction is stated on those FDA labels.

members.name: Iron supplement
members.citation: Ferrous iron chelates tetracyclines and fluoroquinolones and reduces levothyroxine absorption; the interaction is stated on those FDA labels.

members.name: Zinc supplement
members.citation: Divalent zinc chelates fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines; the interaction is stated on those FDA labels.

members.name: Activated charcoal
members.citation: Activated charcoal adsorbs co-ingested drugs nonspecifically; this is the basis of its use in overdose care.

members.name: Psyllium fibre
members.citation: Bulk-forming fibre delays and can reduce absorption of co-ingested drugs; stated in psyllium product labelling.

members.name: Tobacco smoking
members.citation: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in tobacco smoke induce CYP1A2; smoking is the FDA table's non-drug CYP1A2 inducer, and nicotine itself is not the inducer.

members.name: Ethanol (chronic intake)
members.citation: Chronic ethanol induces CYP2E1; described in the ethanol-acetaminophen bioactivation literature.

members.name: Cruciferous vegetables (charbroiled/indole-rich diet)
members.citation: Indole-3-carbinol-rich and charbroiled diets induce CYP1A2; described in the diet-CYP1A2 literature.

members.name: Kratom (mitragynine)
members.citation: Mitragynine inhibits CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 in vitro and is a partial mu-opioid agonist; described in the kratom pharmacology literature.

members.name: Sceletium tortuosum (kanna, mesembrine)
members.citation: Mesembrine is a serotonin reuptake inhibitor and PDE4 inhibitor in vitro; described in the Sceletium pharmacology literature.

classRules.mechanism: MAO inhibition plus an indirect monoamine releasing agent
classRules.evidence: mechanism-class pairing of two labelled pharmacologies
classRules.citation: MAO-inhibitor FDA labels state the contraindication with indirect sympathomimetics and tyramine-rich food.

classRules.mechanism: MAO inhibition plus serotonin reuptake inhibition
classRules.evidence: mechanism-class pairing of two labelled pharmacologies
classRules.citation: MAO-inhibitor and SSRI FDA labels both state the serotonin-syndrome contraindication and the required washout.

classRules.mechanism: MAO inhibition plus increased serotonin precursor supply
classRules.citation: MAO-inhibitor FDA labels state the serotonergic precaution; the precursor route is basic monoamine biochemistry.

classRules.mechanism: serotonin reuptake inhibition plus increased precursor supply
classRules.citation: SSRI FDA labels state the serotonergic precaution with other serotonergic agents.
Triptan and SSRI FDA labels both state the serotonergic precaution.

classRules.mechanism: P-glycoprotein inhibition raising a P-gp substrate's exposure
classRules.citation: FDA, Drug Development and Drug Interactions: Table of Substrates, Inhibitors and Inducers (US Government work, public domain).

classRules.mechanism: intestinal/hepatic OATP inhibition changing a substrate's uptake
classRules.citation: FDA, Drug Development and Drug Interactions: Table of Substrates, Inhibitors and Inducers (US Government work, public domain).

classRules.mechanism: two independent antiplatelet mechanisms in the same stack
classRules.citation: Antiplatelet FDA labels state the additive bleeding mechanism.

classRules.mechanism: vitamin K supply opposing a vitamin K antagonist
classRules.citation: The warfarin FDA label states the dietary vitamin K interaction.

classRules.evidence: absorption mechanism stated on the affected drug's label
classRules.citation: FDA, Drug Development and Drug Interactions: Table of Substrates, Inhibitors and Inducers (US Government work, public domain).

classRules.mechanism: nonspecific adsorption reducing absorption of a co-ingested drug
classRules.citation: Activated-charcoal and bulk-fibre labelling state the adsorption mechanism.
